explanation: American table manners strongly favor quiet eating - chewing with your mouth closed and avoiding noise from food or cutlery is a basic expectation taught from childhood. Slurping noodles or soup loudly is seen as careless or poor manners, the opposite of the social approval the same sound gets in Japan or China.
local_tip: Twirl noodles onto a fork or spoon and eat quietly; the rule relaxes a bit at a ramen or pho shop among people who expect slurping, but quiet eating is the safe default elsewhere.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is seen as a compliment to the chef and is expected at ramen and soba shops.
Slurping noodles is common and signals enjoyment, though it's toned down in more formal dining.
Pasta is eaten quietly, twirled onto a fork without noise; slurping is seen as uncivilized.
